# m68k-asm reference index

Motorola 680x0 instructions (68000 through 68060, plus FPU) and the vasm Motorola-syntax
directives used for Amiga code, with Amiga program-structure guides.

- [Sources](SOURCE.md) · [Errata](errata.md)

## Guides

- [Addressing modes](topics/addressing-modes.md) — Every 680x0 operand is either implied by the opcode (MOVEQ data, quick counts) or an *effective address* (EA) encoded as a 3-bit mode plus a 3-bit register field, followed by...
- [Amiga program structure: hunks, startup and exit](topics/amiga-program-structure.md) — How an assembled program looks to AmigaDOS, what the registers hold when it starts from the Shell (CLI) or from Workbench, and a minimal startup/exit that is correct for both.
- [Condition codes](topics/condition-codes.md) — The low byte of the status register (the CCR) holds five flags that almost every data instruction updates and that Bcc, DBcc, Scc and TRAPcc test.
- [680x0 CPU models on the Amiga](topics/cpu-models.md) — Amiga code written and tested on an A500 (68000) often crashes on an A1200, A4000 or an accelerated machine.
- [Calling AmigaOS libraries from assembler](topics/library-calls.md) — Every OS function is reached through a library base pointer and a negative offset (LVO).
- [Structure offsets: NDK include macros and vasm counters](topics/macros-and-structures.md) — OS structures are described in the NDK asm includes with macros from `exec/types.i`; your own structures can use the same macros or vasm's RS/SO/FO/OFFSET directives.
- [Size and speed idioms](topics/optimisation.md) — Classic 68000 idioms, each with the reason it is equivalent and what it saves.
- [vasm and vlink: assembling and linking Amiga code](topics/vasm-vlink.md) — Two build flows exist around AmigaScope.

## Instruction files

- [68000 instructions: arithmetic and compare](instructions/arithmetic.md) — Notation (sizes, CCR symbols, mode names) as in data movement.
- [68000 instructions: BCD arithmetic](instructions/bcd.md) — Notation (sizes, CCR symbols, mode names) as in data movement.
- [68000 instructions: single-bit operations](instructions/bit.md) — Notation (sizes, CCR symbols, mode names) as in data movement.
- [68020+ instructions, extensions and FPU](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md) — Notation (sizes, CCR symbols, mode names) as in data movement.
- [68000 instructions: data movement](instructions/data-movement.md) — Notation used in every instruction file: `<ea>` = effective address; sizes B/W/L; CCR table `*` = set from the result, `-` = unchanged, `0`/`1` = forced, `U` = undefined.
- [68000 instructions: logic](instructions/logic.md) — Notation (sizes, CCR symbols, mode names) as in data movement.
- [68000 instructions: program control](instructions/program-control.md) — Notation (sizes, CCR symbols, mode names) as in data movement.
- [68000 instructions: shifts and rotates](instructions/shift-rotate.md) — Notation (sizes, CCR symbols, mode names) as in data movement.
- [680x0 instructions: traps, exceptions and supervisor control](instructions/system.md) — Notation (sizes, CCR symbols, mode names) as in data movement.

## Directive files

- [vasm directives: conditional assembly](directives/conditional.md) — vasm reads the source ONCE.
- [vasm directives: data, space and alignment](directives/data.md) — Size qualifiers used below: `.b` 8 bit, `.w` 16, `.l` 32, `.q` 64, `.s` IEEE single (32), `.d` IEEE double (64), `.x` IEEE extended (96), `.p` packed decimal (96).
- [vasm directives: include files and output naming](directives/include-and-output.md) — **Search order for INCLUDE and INCBIN (vasm manual, confirmed by tests):** 1.
- [vasm directives: messages, listing, options and CPU control](directives/listing-and-misc.md) — Listing directives only matter when a listing is requested with `-L <file>`.
- [vasm directives: macros and repetition](directives/macros-repeat.md) — A macro must be defined before its first call (single pass: an earlier call is "unknown mnemonic", tested).
- [vasm directives: sections and origin](directives/sections.md) — Motorola-syntax vasm (`vasmm68k_mot`).
- [vasm directives: structure and stack-frame offsets](directives/structures.md) — Three independent counters generate offset symbols without emitting bytes: `__RS` (RS family, Devpac style), `__SO` (SO family) and `__FO` (FO family, counts DOWN for LINK frames).
- [vasm directives: symbols, linkage and local labels](directives/symbols.md) — Source-line rules (mot syntax): a label starts in column 1 or ends with `:`; a mnemonic or directive must NOT start in column 1.

## Instructions (alphabetical)

- `68020 extensions to 68000 instructions` — Branch, check, link and test instructions that gain wider operands on 68020+. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#68020-extensions-to-68000-instructions)
- `ABCD` — Add source, destination and X in decimal, storing the result in the destination. → [instructions/bcd.md](instructions/bcd.md#abcd)
- `ADD` — Add source to destination; X and C receive the carry, V the signed overflow. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#add)
- `ADDA` — Add to an address register; a word source is sign-extended and the CCR is not changed. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#adda)
- `ADDI` — Add an immediate value (same size as the operation) to a data register or memory. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#addi)
- `ADDQ` — Add an immediate value 1-8 to the destination. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#addq)
- `ADDX` — Add source plus the X bit to destination, for multi-precision addition. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#addx)
- `AND` — Bitwise AND of source into destination (mask bits off). → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#and)
- `ANDI` — AND an immediate mask (same size as the operation) into a data register or memory. → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#andi)
- `ANDI to CCR` — Clear the condition code bits whose mask bit is 0; the others are unchanged. → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#andi-to-ccr)
- `ANDI to SR` — AND a word mask into the whole status register (system byte and CCR). → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#andi-to-sr)
- `ASL, ASR` — Arithmetic shift: left fills with zeros and flags sign changes, right keeps the sign bit. → [instructions/shift-rotate.md](instructions/shift-rotate.md#asl-asr)
- `Availability on 68030, 68040 and 68060` — Which 68020 additions are missing or software-emulated on later CPUs. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#availability-on-68030-68040-and-68060)
- `Bcc` — Branch to the label if condition cc is true, otherwise continue with the next instruction. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#bcc)
- `BCHG` — Test a bit (old state to Z), then invert it. → [instructions/bit.md](instructions/bit.md#bchg)
- `BCLR` — Test a bit (old state to Z), then clear it to 0. → [instructions/bit.md](instructions/bit.md#bclr)
- `BFEXTU, BFEXTS` — Extract a bit field into Dn, zero-extended (BFEXTU) or sign-extended (BFEXTS) to 32 bits. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#bfextu-bfexts)
- `BFFFO` — Find the first 1 bit (from the MSB end) of a bit field and return its offset in Dn. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#bfffo)
- `BFINS` — Insert the low `width` bits of Dn into a bit field. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#bfins)
- `BFTST, BFSET, BFCLR, BFCHG` — Test a bit field (N, Z), then leave it, set it, clear it or invert it. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#bftst-bfset-bfclr-bfchg)
- `BKPT` — Run a breakpoint-acknowledge cycle (number 0-7), then take the illegal-instruction trap. → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#bkpt)
- `BRA` — Branch unconditionally (PC-relative, so position-independent). → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#bra)
- `BSET` — Test a bit (old state to Z), then set it to 1. → [instructions/bit.md](instructions/bit.md#bset)
- `BSR` — Push the return address (longword) and branch to a subroutine PC-relatively. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#bsr)
- `BTST` — Test one bit and report its old state in Z; the operand is not changed. → [instructions/bit.md](instructions/bit.md#btst)
- `CALLM, RTM` — Call a module through a module descriptor and return from it (68020 modules). → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#callm-rtm)
- `CAS, CAS2` — Compare memory with Dc: if equal store Du there, else copy the memory value into Dc. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#cas-cas2)
- `CHK` — Trap (vector 6) if Dn is negative or greater than the signed upper bound at `<ea>`. → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#chk)
- `CHK2, CMP2` — Check Rn against a bounds pair at `<ea>`: CHK2 traps (vector 6), CMP2 only sets flags. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#chk2-cmp2)
- `CINV, CPUSH` — Invalidate cache entries (CINV), or write pending data-cache lines out first (CPUSH). → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#cinv-cpush)
- `CLR` — Set the operand to zero. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#clr)
- `CMP` — Set the flags for Dn - source without storing the result. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#cmp)
- `CMPA` — Set the flags for An - source using all 32 bits; a word source is sign-extended first. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#cmpa)
- `CMPI` — Set the flags for destination - immediate data without changing the destination. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#cmpi)
- `CMPM` — Compare two memory operands addressed by postincrement (flags for (Ax) - (Ay)). → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#cmpm)
- `DBcc` — Loop primitive: if cc is false, decrement Dn.w and branch unless it became -1. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#dbcc)
- `DIVS, DIVU` — Divide 32-bit Dn by a 16-bit source: quotient in the low word, remainder in the high. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#divs-divu)
- `DIVS.L, DIVU.L` — Long division: quotient in Dq; remainder in Dr for the `Dr:Dq` forms. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#divsl-divul)
- `EOR` — Exclusive-OR a data register into the destination (toggle bits). → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#eor)
- `EORI` — Exclusive-OR an immediate mask into a data register or memory. → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#eori)
- `EORI to CCR` — Invert the condition code bits whose mask bit is 1. → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#eori-to-ccr)
- `EORI to SR` — Invert the status register bits whose mask bit is 1. → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#eori-to-sr)
- `EXG` — Exchange the full 32-bit contents of two registers (data/data, address/address or mixed). → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#exg)
- `EXT` — Sign-extend a byte to a word (EXT.W) or a word to a long (EXT.L) in a data register. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#ext)
- `EXTB` — Sign-extend the low byte of Dn to 32 bits in one step. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#extb)
- `FBcc` — Branch (or loop, set a byte, trap) on one of 32 floating-point conditions from the FPSR. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#fbcc)
- `FMOVE` — Move a value to or from an FPU data register (converting it) or FPCR/FPSR/FPIAR. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#fmove)
- `FMOVECR` — Load a constant from the FPU's ROM into FPn. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#fmovecr)
- `FMOVEM` — Save or restore several FP data registers (12 bytes each) or control registers in one go. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#fmovem)
- `FPU (68881, 68882, 68040, 68060)` — Floating-point instructions of the 68881/68882 and the on-chip 68040/68060 FPU. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#fpu-68881-68882-68040-68060)
- `FSAVE, FRESTORE` — Save or restore the FPU's internal (user-invisible) state as a state frame. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#fsave-frestore)
- `ILLEGAL` — Force an illegal-instruction exception (vector 4) with the reserved opcode $4AFC. → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#illegal)
- `JMP` — Continue execution at the effective address. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#jmp)
- `JSR` — Push the return address and continue at the effective address. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#jsr)
- `LEA` — Compute an effective address and load it into an address register without touching memory. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#lea)
- `LINK` — Push An, point An at the new stack top, then add a negative offset to SP for locals. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#link)
- `LSL, LSR` — Logical shift: zeros come in, the last bit shifted out goes to C and X. → [instructions/shift-rotate.md](instructions/shift-rotate.md#lsl-lsr)
- `MOVE` — Copy the source operand to the destination and set N and Z from the value copied. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#move)
- `MOVE from CCR` — Copy the condition codes, zero-extended to a word, to the destination. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#move-from-ccr)
- `MOVE from SR` — Copy the status register to a word destination. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#move-from-sr)
- `MOVE to CCR` — Load X N Z V C from bits 4-0 of a word operand; the system byte of SR is untouched. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#move-to-ccr)
- `MOVE to SR` — Load the whole status register: trace, supervisor, interrupt mask and condition codes. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#move-to-sr)
- `MOVE USP` — Read or set the user stack pointer from supervisor mode. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#move-usp)
- `MOVE16` — Copy one 16-byte block ("line") between 16-byte-aligned addresses using burst transfers. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#move16)
- `MOVEA` — Load an address register; a word source is sign-extended and no flags change. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#movea)
- `MOVEC` — Copy a CPU control register to or from a general register (always 32 bits). → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#movec)
- `MOVEM` — Save or restore a set of registers to or from consecutive memory in one instruction. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#movem)
- `MOVEP` — Move a word or long to/from every other byte of an 8-bit peripheral, high byte first. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#movep)
- `MOVEQ` — Load an 8-bit signed constant (-128..127) sign-extended into all 32 bits of Dn. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#moveq)
- `MOVES` — Move data to or from memory in the address space selected by DFC (write) or SFC (read). → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#moves)
- `MULS, MULU` — Multiply the low words of source and Dn (signed or unsigned) into a full 32-bit Dn. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#muls-mulu)
- `MULS.L, MULU.L` — Multiply 32 x 32 bits, keeping the low 32 bits in Dl or the full 64 bits in Dh:Dl. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#mulsl-mulul)
- `NBCD` — Subtract the operand and X from zero in decimal (ten's complement if X=0, nine's if X=1). → [instructions/bcd.md](instructions/bcd.md#nbcd)
- `NEG` — Replace the operand with its two's complement (0 - operand). → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#neg)
- `NEGX` — Subtract the operand and the X bit from zero, for multi-precision negation. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#negx)
- `NOP` — Do nothing (opcode $4E71), except let the PC advance. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#nop)
- `NOT` — Replace the operand with its one's complement (invert every bit). → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#not)
- `OR` — Bitwise inclusive OR of source into destination (force bits on). → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#or)
- `ORI` — OR an immediate mask (same size as the operation) into a data register or memory. → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#ori)
- `ORI to CCR` — Set the condition code bits whose mask bit is 1; the others are unchanged. → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#ori-to-ccr)
- `ORI to SR` — OR a word mask into the whole status register. → [instructions/logic.md](instructions/logic.md#ori-to-sr)
- `PACK, UNPK` — Convert between one packed BCD byte and two unpacked digit bytes, with an adjustment. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#pack-unpk)
- `PEA` — Compute an effective address and push it as a longword on the stack. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#pea)
- `RESET` — Pulse the RESET line for external devices; the CPU continues with the next instruction. → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#reset)
- `ROL, ROR` — Rotate without X: bits leaving one end re-enter at the other; C gets the last bit moved. → [instructions/shift-rotate.md](instructions/shift-rotate.md#rol-ror)
- `ROXL, ROXR` — Rotate through X: operand and X form a 9/17/33-bit ring; C and X get the last bit out. → [instructions/shift-rotate.md](instructions/shift-rotate.md#roxl-roxr)
- `RTD` — Return from a subroutine and add a signed 16-bit value to SP to drop stacked arguments. → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#rtd)
- `RTE` — Return from an exception: restore SR and PC from the stack (and discard the 68010+ frame). → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#rte)
- `RTR` — Pop a word into the CCR, then pop the return address into the PC. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#rtr)
- `RTS` — Pop a longword return address into the PC. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#rts)
- `SBCD` — Subtract source and X from destination in decimal (dst - src - X -> dst). → [instructions/bcd.md](instructions/bcd.md#sbcd)
- `Scc` — Set a byte to $FF if condition cc is true, otherwise to $00. → [instructions/program-control.md](instructions/program-control.md#scc)
- `STOP` — Load SR with the immediate word and halt until an interrupt, trace or reset exception. → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#stop)
- `SUB` — Subtract source from destination (dst - src -> dst); X and C receive the borrow. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#sub)
- `SUBA` — Subtract from an address register; a word source is sign-extended and no flags change. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#suba)
- `SUBI` — Subtract an immediate value (same size as the operation) from a data register or memory. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#subi)
- `SUBQ` — Subtract an immediate value 1-8 from the destination. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#subq)
- `SUBX` — Subtract source and the X bit from destination, for multi-precision subtraction. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#subx)
- `SWAP` — Exchange the upper and lower 16-bit halves of a data register. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#swap)
- `TAS` — Test a byte (N, Z from its old value) and set its bit 7 in one indivisible bus cycle. → [instructions/bit.md](instructions/bit.md#tas)
- `TRAP` — Enter supervisor mode through exception vector 32 + n (n = 0..15). → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#trap)
- `TRAPcc` — Take the TRAPcc exception (vector 7) if cc is true; the operand is for the handler. → [instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md](instructions/cpu-68020-plus.md#trapcc)
- `TRAPV` — Take the TRAPV exception (vector 7) if V is set; otherwise do nothing. → [instructions/system.md](instructions/system.md#trapv)
- `TST` — Set N and Z from the operand and clear V and C. → [instructions/arithmetic.md](instructions/arithmetic.md#tst)
- `UNLK` — Discard a LINK frame: SP = An, then pop the old An. → [instructions/data-movement.md](instructions/data-movement.md#unlk)

## Directives (alphabetical)

- `ALIGN` — Pad with zero bytes until the low `bits` bits of the address are zero. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#align)
- `ASSERT` — Error when the expression is false; only in newer vasm, not in the bundled builds. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#assert)
- `BASEREG` — Access labels as offsets from a base address you have loaded into An yourself. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#basereg)
- `BLK` — Same as `dcb.<size> <count>,<fill>`, for sources from other assemblers. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#blk)
- `BSS` — Switch to vasm's default uninitialised section (manual: `section bss,bss`). → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#bss)
- `BSS_C` — Switch to an uninitialised section loaded into chip RAM. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#bss_c)
- `BSS_F` — Switch to an uninitialised section that must load into fast RAM. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#bss_f)
- `CARGS` — Define stack-argument offsets: first symbol = offset, each next = previous + its size. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#cargs)
- `CLRFO` — Set `__FO` to 0. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#clrfo)
- `CLRSO` — Set `__SO` to 0. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#clrso)
- `CNOP` — Pad to a multiple of `alignment`, then add `offset` more padding bytes. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#cnop)
- `CODE` — Switch to vasm's default code section (manual: same as `section code,code`). → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#code)
- `CODE_C` — Switch to a code section loaded into chip RAM. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#code_c)
- `CODE_F` — Switch to a code section that must load into fast RAM. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#code_f)
- `COMM` — Create a common (shared, linker-allocated) data block of `size` bytes. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#comm)
- `COMMENT` — Ignore the rest of the line. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#comment)
- `CSEG` — Switch to the default code section; a synonym of CODE for other assemblers. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#cseg)
- `DATA` — Switch to vasm's default initialised-data section (manual: `section data,data`). → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#data)
- `DATA_C` — Switch to an initialised-data section loaded into chip RAM. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#data_c)
- `DATA_F` — Switch to an initialised-data section that must load into fast RAM. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#data_f)
- `DB` — Same as `dc.b`, for ArgAsm/BAsm/Macro68/ProAsm sources. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#db)
- `DC` — Store integer, string or float constants into the current section. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#dc)
- `DCB` — Emit `count` elements filled with `fill` (default 0). → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#dcb)
- `DL` — Same as `dc.l`, for ArgAsm/BAsm/Macro68/ProAsm sources. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#dl)
- `DR` — Store `exp - address_of_this_element` for each operand. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#dr)
- `DS` — Reserve `count` elements of space, zero-filled. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#ds)
- `DSEG` — Switch to the default data section; a synonym of DATA (from the vasm manual, not prb28). → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#dseg)
- `DW` — Same as `dc.w`, for ArgAsm/BAsm/Macro68/ProAsm sources. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#dw)
- `DX` — Reserve zeroed space that vasm tries to keep out of the file (data-bss part of a section). → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#dx)
- `ECHO` — Print strings and expression values on one line. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#echo)
- `EINLINE` — End an INLINE block; local labels from before the block are visible again. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#einline)
- `ELIF` — A real else-if in newer vasm (manual); the bundled 1.8k and 1.9 builds do not know it. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#elif)
- `ELSE` — Switch to the opposite branch of the current conditional block. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#else)
- `ELSEIF` — Same as ELSE; any operand is IGNORED (vasm manual, tested). → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#elseif)
- `END` — Stop assembling; every following line is ignored. → [directives/include-and-output.md](directives/include-and-output.md#end)
- `ENDB` — End a BASEREG block for that register. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#endb)
- `ENDIF, ENDC` — Close the innermost conditional block (the two names are identical). → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#endif-endc)
- `ENDM` — End a macro definition. → [directives/macros-repeat.md](directives/macros-repeat.md#endm)
- `ENDR` — End a REPT block. → [directives/macros-repeat.md](directives/macros-repeat.md#endr)
- `EQU` — Define a constant symbol; defining it a second time is an error. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#equ)
- `EQUR` — Give a data or address register an alias name. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#equr)
- `EREM` — End a REM block; assembly continues on the next line. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#erem)
- `EVEN` — Pad with one zero byte if the address is odd (same as `cnop 0,2`). → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#even)
- `FAIL` — Stop with an error (error 20) showing the message; no output file is written. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#fail)
- `FAR` — Switch small-data (and `near code`) mode off; references are absolute again. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#far)
- `FEQU` — Define a floating-point constant symbol (the size extension is ignored). → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#fequ)
- `FEQUR` — Give an FPU register an alias name; define it before use. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#fequr)
- `FO` — Move `__FO` down by size x count, then give `label` the new (negative) value. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#fo)
- `FPU` — Enable 68881/68882 FPU instructions with coprocessor ID `cpID` (1 for 68040/060 FPUs). → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#fpu)
- `FREG` — Name an FPU register list for FMOVEM (`fp0-fp7`, `fp2/fp4`, or an 8-bit mask). → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#freg)
- `IDNT` — Set the module name stored in the object file. → [directives/include-and-output.md](directives/include-and-output.md#idnt)
- `IF` — Assemble the block if the expression is non-zero. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#if)
- `IF1, IFP1` — Pass-1 test kept for old sources; always true in vasm (warning 1026). → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#if1-ifp1)
- `IF2` — Pass-2 test kept for old sources; always false in vasm (warning 1027). → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#if2)
- `IFB` — Assemble the block if the operand field is empty (a comment is allowed). → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifb)
- `IFC` — Assemble the block if the two strings are identical. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifc)
- `IFD` — Assemble the block if the symbol is defined at this point of the source. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifd)
- `IFEQ` — Assemble the block if the expression is zero. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifeq)
- `IFGE` — Assemble the block if the expression is zero or greater. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifge)
- `IFGT` — Assemble the block if the expression is greater than zero. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifgt)
- `IFLE` — Assemble the block if the expression is zero or less. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifle)
- `IFLT` — Assemble the block if the expression is less than zero. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#iflt)
- `IFMACROD` — Assemble the block if a macro of that name is defined. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifmacrod)
- `IFMACROND` — Assemble the block if no macro of that name is defined. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifmacrond)
- `IFNB` — Assemble the block if the operand field is not empty. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifnb)
- `IFNC` — Assemble the block if the two strings differ. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifnc)
- `IFND` — Assemble the block if the symbol is not (yet) defined. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifnd)
- `IFNE` — Assemble the block if the expression is non-zero (same as IF). → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#ifne)
- `IIF` — Assemble a single statement if the expression is non-zero; no `endc` is used. → [directives/conditional.md](directives/conditional.md#iif)
- `INCBIN` — Insert the raw bytes of a file at this position. → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#incbin)
- `INCDIR` — Add a directory to the include search list. → [directives/include-and-output.md](directives/include-and-output.md#incdir)
- `INCLUDE` — Insert another source file at this point. → [directives/include-and-output.md](directives/include-and-output.md#include)
- `INITNEAR` — Emit `lea _LinkerDB,An` for the current NEAR base register (vlink resolves it). → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#initnear)
- `INLINE` — Start a block whose local labels are isolated from those around it. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#inline)
- `LIST` — Resume writing lines to the listing file (only with `-L <file>`). → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#list)
- `LLEN` — Set the listing line length; has no effect (warning 1012, tested). → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#llen)
- `LOCAL` — Start a new block of local labels; only in newer vasm, not in the bundled builds. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#local)
- `Local labels` — A label starting with `.` or ending with `$` is local to its enclosing global labels. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#local-labels)
- `MACHINE` — Switch the instruction set for the following code. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#machine)
- `MACRO` — Define a macro; the body runs until ENDM. → [directives/macros-repeat.md](directives/macros-repeat.md#macro)
- `MEXIT` — Leave the current macro expansion immediately. → [directives/macros-repeat.md](directives/macros-repeat.md#mexit)
- `MSOURCE` — Choose whether debug line info inside macros points at the macro body or at the call line. → [directives/macros-repeat.md](directives/macros-repeat.md#msource)
- `NARG` — Number of arguments passed to the current macro; -1 outside any macro (tested). → [directives/macros-repeat.md](directives/macros-repeat.md#narg)
- `NEAR` — Enable small-data mode: references into the `__MERGED` section become `(offset,An)`. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#near)
- `NOLIST` — Leave this and the following lines out of the listing file. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#nolist)
- `NOPAGE` — Never emit form feeds in the listing file. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#nopage)
- `NREF` — Import a symbol that may be accessed base-relative (small data). → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#nref)
- `ODD` — Align to an odd address (same as `cnop 1,2`). → [directives/data.md](directives/data.md#odd)
- `OFFSET` — Open a dummy section whose labels become structure offsets and emit no bytes. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#offset)
- `OPT` — Set Devpac-style assembler options from inside the source. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#opt)
- `ORG` — Assemble the following code for a fixed absolute address. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#org)
- `OUTPUT` — Set the output file name when none was given with `-o`. → [directives/include-and-output.md](directives/include-and-output.md#output)
- `PAGE` — Start a new listing page; not implemented in vasm. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#page)
- `PLEN` — Set the listing page length; accepted and ignored. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#plen)
- `POPSECTION` — Return to the section most recently saved with PUSHSECTION. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#popsection)
- `PRINTT` — Print text to stdout during assembly, one line per string; quotes are optional. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#printt)
- `PRINTV` — Print each value as hex, decimal, ASCII and binary on its own line. → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#printv)
- `PUBLIC` — Mark symbols external: exported if defined in this file, imported otherwise. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#public)
- `PUSHSECTION` — Save the current section on vasm's section stack. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#pushsection)
- `REG` — Name a register list for MOVEM. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#reg)
- `REM` — Ignore every following line until EREM (block comment). → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#rem)
- `REPT` — Assemble the block up to ENDR `count` times. → [directives/macros-repeat.md](directives/macros-repeat.md#rept)
- `RORG` — Move the program counter to an offset from the start of the current section. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#rorg)
- `RS` — Give `label` the current `__RS` value, then advance `__RS` by size x count. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#rs)
- `RSEVEN` — Align `__RS` to an even value (newer vasm manual); unknown mnemonic on the bundled builds. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#rseven)
- `RSRESET` — Set `__RS` to 0 before starting a new structure. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#rsreset)
- `RSSET` — Set `__RS` to a constant, e.g. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#rsset)
- `SECTION` — Start a section, or switch back to one with the same name, type and memory attribute. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#section)
- `SET` — Define a symbol that may be assigned again later. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#set)
- `SETFO` — Set `__FO` to a constant expression, e.g. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#setfo)
- `SETSO` — Set `__SO` to a constant expression. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#setso)
- `SHOWOFFSET` — Print the current section offset, preceded by the optional text (PhxAss compatibility). → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#showoffset)
- `SO` — Give `label` the current `__SO` value, then advance `__SO` by size x count. → [directives/structures.md](directives/structures.md#so)
- `SPC` — Insert blank lines in the listing; has no effect (warning 1012, tested). → [directives/listing-and-misc.md](directives/listing-and-misc.md#spc)
- `TEXT` — Switch to the default code section; a synonym of CODE. → [directives/sections.md](directives/sections.md#text)
- `TTL` — Title directive whose meaning depends on the vasm version. → [directives/include-and-output.md](directives/include-and-output.md#ttl)
- `WEAK` — Export a symbol that any normal global definition of the same name overrides. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#weak)
- `XDEF` — Export symbols so other objects can reference them at link time. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#xdef)
- `XREF` — Declare symbols that another object or library defines. → [directives/symbols.md](directives/symbols.md#xref)
